text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Right-wing Disy is to back Limassol mayor Antonis Haggipavlou during municipal elections.
- Italian porn star Ciccolina arrives in Cyprus, dressed, for a change.
- The government is to set up a detective unit to fight money laundering.
- Attorney-general rules only the Cyprus flag can fly at the University of Cyprus.
- Turks ban Ledra Palace contacts in crossing row.
- Commerce Minister Kyriakos Christofi washes his hands of any responsibility in the financial scandal at the Cyprus electricity authority.
- Communist parties of Cyprus and Greece express concern that a deviation from the United Nations framework to achieve a settlement on Cyprus could lead to a partition.

- Communist Akel deputy says directors of state-run electricity authority should be suspended pending inquiries into claims of irregular procedures adopted for endorsing a tender for turbines and boilers.
- Britain and America have started contacts ahead of initiatives they are expected to undertake to breach the deadlock on the Cyprus problem.
- Limassol marina harbour plan is called off because of legal complications.
- The government puts new recruitments in the civil service on hold.
- Right-wing Democratic Rally starts intensive consultations for the selection of its candidates in the municipal elections.
- Deputy police chief says there is no evidence to back up claims made by the drugs squad director that members of the squad are in cahoots with dealers.
